html:
The Jones Act, signed on 2 March 1917, made the people of Puerto Rico citizens of the United States. It also gave the island an elected senate.

It came weeks before the US entered World War I, and many Puerto Ricans were soon drafted. The island's leaders had asked for more self rule, and some had wanted independence instead of citizenship.

Citizenship let Puerto Ricans move freely to the mainland, which led to the great migration to New York after World War II. But Puerto Rico stayed a territory without a vote in Congress or for president, a status the US Supreme Court had upheld in the Insular Cases and which led to the Commonwealth of 1952.
sum: The Jones Act, signed on 2 March 1917, made the people of Puerto Rico citizens of the United States. It also gave the island an elected senate.
